source.title: When the Mall Taught Men How to Dress: J.Crew, Banana Republic & Gap

tips.text: Relax classic preppy clothes: let an oxford wrinkle, push up sleeves, wear loafers with faded jeans or a sweatshirt under a blazer.
tips.why: Good prep should look lived-in, not arranged.

tips.text: Choose pieces that get better with age: a suede jacket, a slightly rumpled linen shirt, an olive field jacket, brown loafers that have been walked in.
tips.why: Clothes that acquire character look personal.

tips.text: Straight blue jeans, a white tee, a grey sweatshirt and simple sneakers take most men a long way if the proportions are right.
tips.why: Simple basics work when they fit well.

tips.text: Don't make everything skin tight: let jeans fall straight from the hip, chinos have room in the thigh and an oxford blouse slightly at the waist.
tips.why: A little ease looks more natural and current than vacuum-sealed slim fits.

tips.text: Start with pieces that survive every trend: good jeans, chinos, an oxford shirt, knitwear, a casual jacket and simple shoes, then add one or two personal pieces.
tips.why: A solid base plus a bit of personality beats chasing trends.

tips.text: Build a wardrobe slowly, one considered piece at a time, rather than in one big online order.
tips.why: You learn what works and buy less.

tips.text: When buying vintage or second-hand, check the garment's measurements rather than the size on the label, and favour natural fabrics.
tips.why: Sizing changes over the years; natural fibres last.

tips.text: An earthy palette of tobacco, olive, cream, khaki and brown, with linen and suede, gives a worldly, understated look.
tips.why: These tones all mix and look quietly expensive.

tips.text: Pleated trousers in cream or khaki bring ease and a vintage touch to casual outfits.
